speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The introduction of this corporate structure, known as the variable capital company, or "VCC", will be a game changer for Singapore’s fund management industry as it will allow us to capture value from the full fund management value chain.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The VCC regime will strengthen our position as the Asian hub for fund domiciliation and management.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is already recognised as a leading Asian fund management hub.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Almost $7 in every $10 under management are invested into the Asia-Pacific region, reflecting Singapore's role as a key node for global fund managers and investors to invest in the region’s growth opportunities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Industry Transformation Map (ITM) for financial services has set out Singapore’s strategy to be an Asian hub for fund management and domiciliation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Besides the introduction of VCC to encourage fund domiciliation activities in Singapore, we are deepening fund management capabilities in specialty and alternative investments to complement our strengths in portfolio management, trading and research.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are also building a deeper and more diverse capital pool for investment into Asia from Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The VCC structure will complement and expand the existing suite of fund structures available in Singapore, such as the company, the limited partnership and unit trust structures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Taken together, this will provide a comprehensive range of investment fund vehicles and structures to support investors’ needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill takes reference from similar corporate fund structures available in other global investment fund centres, such as Ireland, Luxembourg and the United Kingdom (UK).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has consulted on the VCC framework and the Bill and has engaged extensively with the industry and the public over the past 18 months.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There was broad industry support for the VCC framework and the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MAS has considered all the feedback received and taken it into account where appropriate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, fund managers already conduct a good range of their fund management activities in Singapore – portfolio management, trading and research.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The VCC framework will encourage fund managers to domicile their funds in Singapore, adding domiciliation activities to the fund management activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This, in turn, will establish a full-service fund ecosystem in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Besides the direct value-add contribution, it has significant spillovers to other financial sector activities, such as the trading of foreign exchange, as well as to other service providers, such as lawyers and accountants.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is potential for Singapore to capture a greater share of the full value chain of fund management, particularly in the fund servicing space.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a result, most of the economic benefits generated by service providers to these investment funds accrue outside Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore-based fund managers who domicile funds locally as VCCs can look forward to significant cost economies and fewer cross-border administrative and compliance hurdles through the use of local service providers operating out of just one country.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In contrast, funds domiciled overseas but sold in Singapore typically incur additional costs from having to use multiple service providers across different countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: VCCs would also be able to avail themselves of Singapore’s competitive tax regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Beyond fund managers, the VCC framework will create new business opportunities for lawyers, accountants, tax advisors, fund administrators and custodians in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In practice, VCCs will operate from an office in Singapore and employ Singapore-based corporate secretaries, engage Singapore-based lawyers, fund administrators and so on to facilitate their operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is not the only jurisdiction in this region that has introduced VCC equivalent structures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We need to keep pace with other international fund management centres if we are to capture the additional economic benefits of fund domiciliation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The VCC is a body corporate incorporated under the VCC Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This can be likened to how companies are incorporated under the Companies Act (Cap 50).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The sole object of a VCC is to be a structure for investment funds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The shareholders in a VCC are the fund investors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The board of directors owe duties to act in the best interests of the VCC, and a fund manager must be appointed to manage the VCC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I will now highlight several features of the Bill that will specifically address the needs of investment funds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill caters to an investment fund’s need for flexibility in the use of its capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Unlike companies under the Companies Act (Cap 50), VCCs are able to vary their share capital, without having to seek investors’ approval.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is a common feature in investment funds and allows investors the flexibility to exit their investments in the fund when they wish to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To safeguard the interests of creditors, VCC shares must generally be issued and redeemed at their net asset value.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is so that liabilities will always be accounted for in the price of issuance and redemption.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In addition, VCCs will be able to pay dividends using capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In contrast, companies under the Companies Act (Cap 50) can only pay dividends out of profits.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This feature is important, as it allows investment funds to meet their dividend payment schedules which may have been agreed upon with investors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill allows a VCC to be established as a standalone fund, or as an umbrella fund with multiple sub-funds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The umbrella with sub-funds structure creates economies of scale, as the sub-funds can share a common board of directors and use the same service providers, including the same fund manager, custodian, auditor and administrative agent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This would benefit fund managers, who may, for example, wish to group their funds, such as their Asian bond fund together with their European equities fund, under a single umbrella VCC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Certain administrative functions can also be consolidated, such as the holding of general meetings and preparation of prospectuses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A sub-fund will have separate assets and liabilities, distinct from other sub-funds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As the sub-funds will not have separate legal personalities, there is the possibility that the assets and liabilities of one sub-fund could be commingled with that of another sub-fund.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under the Bill, any agreement to use the assets of one sub-fund to discharge the liabilities of the umbrella fund, or another sub-fund, would be void.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The rule on the segregation of assets and liabilities of sub-funds will also apply during insolvency.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To ensure ringfencing of a sub-fund’s assets and liabilities in the event of an insolvency, each sub-fund has to be wound up separately.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Alternative funds, such as private equity and real estate funds, are typically structured as closed-end funds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This means that the fund has a fixed number of shares that cannot be redeemed at the election of shareholders, except in limited circumstances, where permitted, by the fund.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In contrast, traditional funds are often structured as open-ended funds, where investors can exit their investments by redeeming their investment units or shares in the fund.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: VCCs are flexible structures, in that they may be constituted as open-ended or closed-end funds, providing a suitable corporate structure for both traditional and alternative strategies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This caters to the diverse needs of the Singapore-based fund management community, which comprises both traditional and alternative managers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Given the growth in the alternative space, it is also important that the VCC structure can be used by alternative managers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Corporate structures can and have been used around the world for unlawful purposes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To mitigate against such risks for VCCs, VCCs must appoint a fund manager that is regulated by MAS to facilitate supervisory oversight on the use of the VCCs for investment funds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Like companies, VCCs will be required to set up Boards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As mentioned earlier, VCC directors will owe fiduciary duties to act in the best interests of the VCC, similar to those owed by a director of a company to the company.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: VCCs offered to retail investors, or that have sub-funds offered to retail investors, will be subject to an additional requirement to have at least three directors on their boards, at least one of whom must be independent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The requirement for an independent director is an additional safeguard to help ensure good governance of retail VCCs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: VCCs will have to prepare financial statements that must be audited.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To cater to the needs of global investors, VCCs will be allowed to prepare their financial statements using not just Singapore accounting standards and principles but also International Financial Reporting Standards and the US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The register of VCC shareholders need not be made public, but must be disclosed to public authorities for regulatory, supervisory and law enforcement purposes upon request.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This arrangement takes into account investors’ need for privacy and is consistent with the practice in other major fund jurisdictions, such as the UK and Ireland.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: VCCs will also be subject to, and supervised for, anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism requirements, in line with international standards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This means that the business opportunities and jobs created for the fund services industry will stem not only from the creation of new funds structured as VCCs, but also from existing overseas funds re-domiciling into Singapore as VCCs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In addition, existing funds domiciled in Singapore as companies, limited partnerships or unit trusts can also restructure to take advantage of the VCC structure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill provisions relating to the insolvency of a VCC and its sub-funds are adapted from the Companies Act (Cap 50).

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: We have seen impressive asset under management (AUM) growth over the years.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: As the Second Minister of Finance recapped just now, we are now home to 700 asset managers.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The introduction of the VCC Bill is timely.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It further strengthens Singapore’s position as a full-service international fund management centre.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, this new corporate structure, tailored for investment funds, should spur co-location of fund managers and fund ancillary services in Singapore by enabling cost economies, ease of administration and compliance for fund managers.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: However, attracting funds to be domiciled in Singapore will not be an easy task.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Other established fund centres, such as Cayman Islands, Republic of Ireland, Luxembourg and recently Hong Kong, come with their own distinct history and value propositions, offering a whole suite of incentives, ranging from tax-free regimes, flexible legislation, accounting flexibility and a real commitment to serving the international fund industry.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Whilst the proposed Singapore VCC structure compares reasonably well against its international peers, catering to investment funds for traditional and alternative strategies, both on an open-ended and closed-ended basis, there will always be inertia to try out a new structure.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: We must, therefore, ensure Singapore's VCC framework offers a unique value proposition.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Conversions to VCC should be allowed to take place with no Singapore tax consequences and should be granted automatically to encourage transition to VCC.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Re-domiciliation incentives could also be provided to encourage fund managers with funds domiciled in offshore jurisdictions to co-locate fund domiciliation with their fund management activities in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The Government should work closely with local champions, such as Dymon Asia, Lion Global Investors, to lead the way for the adoption of VCC for new funds.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: We should drive adoption starting from home base and support early adopters with "early bird" incentives.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The proposed framework allows funds domiciled overseas to be re-domiciled in Singapore as VCCs by registration with the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA).

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: However, the industry has given feedback that more needs to be done to refine policies to better support the conversion of local funds to VCC.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Many industry players find the process for converting existing domestic collective investment structures into VCC cumbersome.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Rightly or wrongly, some actually feel that the restructuring of local funds as VCC appears more difficult than re-domiciliation.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Being a relatively late comer, we should design our VCC framework with a distinct advantage to serve the rapidly growing alternative sector AUM, comprising hedge funds, venture capital, private equity, real estate and infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This would be an excellent window to establish ourselves as a vibrant financing hub to support the next generation of Asian growth companies.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This will require a nuanced understanding of the web of varied local regulations and international tax developments.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For example, one of the issues raised by the industry is the legal identity of sub-funds under the VCC umbrella entity.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Even with safeguards put in place to ensure segregation of assets and liabilities, market players view that giving sub-funds a legal identity would be a more straightforward and effective way to ringfence sub-funds' assets and liabilities in order to facilitate flexible sub-fund set up and closure, or exit.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Importantly, there is a need to cater to structural issues which feed into taxation matters, for example, investments into India via a sub-fund where a Certificate of Residence (COR) is required for claiming tax benefits.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The lack of a legal entity status of sub-funds could potentially hinder fund managers to flexibly structure an umbrella entity with multiple sub-funds with distinct investment objectives.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Thus, one of the VCC’s selling points is its flexibility to pay dividends and redeem shares versus companies with fixed capital.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The notion of variable capital provisions is, therefore, critical to the operations of an investment fund.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Yet, the closure of a VCC's sub-fund seems to mirror the process under the Companies Act, requiring a liquidator to be appointed and involve more formal company liquidation procedure.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Would the Second Minister consider lightening the unwinding process for sub-funds, such as allowing a strike-off if the sub-fund satisfies all the criteria for striking off?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This will improve operational flexibility to promote the usage of a VCC structure.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I applaud MAS for structuring VCC with a robust governance and oversight framework.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: We must invest strongly to nurture a vibrant local ecosystem of fund service providers to enhance the sophistication of our overall system for the long term.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: We must ensure that the expertise required to operate the VCC framework does not constrain our growth.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It could be a game changer for asset management in the Asia Pacific.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In so doing, it aims to enhance the competitiveness of Singapore as a fund management hub.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Another way of looking at this is that the capital of a VCC will always be equal to its net assets, offering flexibility in the distribution and reduction of capital.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is in contrast to the company structure that has restrictions on capital reduction and can only pay dividends out of profits.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The VCC will also allow for a wider variety of accounting standards to be used in preparing financial statements, which may attract more global funds to be domiciled in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I do, however, pose the following questions and requests for clarification.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If so, what safeguards would protect retail investors from the risk that the fund manager would deplete capital by paying dividends from capital rather than profits, a trend that has not been unknown in other jurisdictions that allow VCCs?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: No doubt retail investors would receive explanations about the nature of these funds and they would have visibility of a declining net asset value (NAV), and the matter could thus be left to market forces.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But would regulations impose a duty of care on VCC fund managers to explain this possibility to retail investors?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The MAS consultation paper in 2017 stated: "MAS recognises that tax treatment is one of the considerations for deciding on the domiciliation and management of funds.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Another example, would stamp duty be imposed on transfers of shares in VCCs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When investment managers are deciding where to house their funds, they look for three key things: privacy for their investors, flexibility in their operations, and tax exemptions from the Government.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Until now, we have had no corporate structure providing all of these features.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This means that asset managers based in Singapore have been overseeing funds mostly domiciled in offshore jurisdictions like Cayman Islands.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It allows investment funds to use popular global accounting standards rather than just the Singapore standard.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It allows non-disclosure of the fund’s investors and financial statements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I commend the MAS for taking a consultative approach on this issue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2017, it held a public consultation on the issue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Industry observers and interested citizens provided feedback, and the MAS responded by tweaking its proposal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The final product blends sensible Government with industry expertise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That said, I have some clarifications to make.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The first point relates to the investigation of VCCs for misconduct.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Second Minister clarify in what circumstances would the Ministry investigate the affairs and ownership of a VCC?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What are the processes that the Ministry has in place to ensure that VCCs conduct themselves in a lawful manner?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate that the Second Minister has shared some information about this in her opening speech.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My concern stems primarily from the fact that unlike regular companies in Singapore, VCCs do not need to disclose their list of shareholders or their financial statements to the public.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While this is consistent with how unit trusts are already treated and with what investors expect from an investment fund, it nonetheless limits the level of public scrutiny and places the sole responsibility on the Government to spot and uncover misconduct.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have learnt from the leaks of the Panama Papers and the Paradise Papers that highly secretive company structures can hide unlawful activities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These leaks have triggered worldwide investigations and toppled governments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If this Bill succeeds in its goals and investment funds re-domicile from offshore jurisdictions to Singapore, the gaze of the world will inevitably turn towards our nation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How will we distinguish ourselves from places like the Cayman Islands?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should be concerned about the risks to Singapore's international reputation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Fairly or not, Singapore is already widely labelled as a tax haven.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A 2018 research paper by economics professors from Berkeley and Copenhagen also branded Singapore as a tax haven.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The risks come amid a sustained global push against tax havens.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Entities like the European Union (EU) and the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) have moved to blacklist tax havens, though neither has included Singapore on their lists.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But researchers, reporters and NGOs namedrop us when reporting on this issue nonetheless.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our reputation as a clean, fair and transparent financial hub takes a hit with every mention.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Not to mention that the legitimate concerns about money laundering and fraud, and an ever-pervasive problem in a world of complex financial and corporate arrangements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, the Bill provides little guidance on the scenarios in which the Government would investigate VCCs, their managers and their shareholders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It states that any investigations would be in the interest of the public, creditors or the shareholders, or based on allegations of misconduct.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would be good if the Second Minister can further outline the practices, principles, policies and systems it has in place to safeguard against misconduct related to VCCs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2016, then Senior Minister of State, and now Second Minister Indranee Rajah, said at a conference of investment management professionals that the introduction of VCCs would create more "good jobs" in the professional services sector, including in accounting, legal, compliance, marketing and information technology.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The MAS' public statements in more recent weeks have not addressed similar topics and have instead tailored its message to investment managers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition to what Second Minister Indranee said, VCCs will surely contribute to the Singapore economy by paying corporate registration fees, name registration fees, annual filing fees and legal fees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This direct impact can be measured in dollars and cents.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Given the advantages that come with it, I foresee we will experience a substantial growth in the number of local and international portfolios.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Certainly, it will be a major boost to our status as a regional and international financial hub.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Currently, investment companies impose a number of restrictions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, shareholders' approval is needed for the issuance and redemption of shares and this can result in delays, especially when there are many shareholders.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Furthermore, for company structures with restrictions on capital reduction, dividends may only be paid out of profits.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Such freedom would encourage more fund managers to base their investment activities in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, I am concerned about whether this may give rise to situations where we see more disruptions as a result of investors changing their minds and trying to move in and out of their investments.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We have to consider how it may affect our financial system in terms of systemic risk, and as what hon Member Mr Louis Ng has mentioned, either due to misconduct or market risk, or counterpart risk and its related impact into systemic risks as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will too much freedom lead to a more volatile economy?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Perhaps the Secod Minister can share her views with the House on this.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, in the current global economic climate, and with the volatile political environment in the West, the big movement of funds in an out of an instrument cannot be underestimated.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Hence, fund managers in Singapore who have their funds domiciled in offshore jurisdictions like the Cayman Islands may consider co-locating their fund domiciliation with their fund management activities.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Our stable economy, our political stability, with our pro-business environment and good governance, we already have an edge over many other countries in the provision of financial services.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With the VCC, I am confident that many funds will be happy to move their fund management activities to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: All these could mean jobs for Singaporeans in the support sector or ancillary services.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the Government proactively engage these foreign corporate entities to make the conversion?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We also need to train a talent pool of people when this sector of the business expands.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I also note that the VCC Bill allows for the accommodation of a wider scope of accounting standards in the preparation of financial statements.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This brings to mind the possibility of rejuvenating the accounting industry in Singapore, which is in danger of being edged out by technology.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can we make use of this opportunity to upskill our accountants?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: When new accounting standards are incorporated, it is inevitable for discrepancies to arise.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, perhaps local accountants can get acquainted with the new standards and serve as bridges.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Being equipped with professional financial knowhow, they will also be in a better position to support our endeavour to become an exemplary global fund management centre.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I believe our Finance Ministry and MAS would be working with the universities to address this new demand for people in a specialised area, from accounting to fund management and to custodian services.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Could the Second Minister confirm if this is being addressed?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We must make use of this opportunity to make the most out of it.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I support the aims behind this Bill, which is really to propel Singapore as a premier international fund management centre.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I fully agree with the hon Second Minister's characterisation of this Bill as a game changer.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Like the hon Member Mr Louis Ng, I also applaud MAS' move in conducting public consultation on the proposed framework for the draft Bill over 18 months and incorporating feedback into the Bill where appropriate before this Bill was tabled.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Singapore's ability to attract and domicile funds is significantly advanced.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Off the top of my head, I believe about 100 countries have DTAs with Singapore.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There are significant restrictions in using companies as structures for funds, however.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The hon Member Mr Sakitiandi Supaat mentioned about it.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There are limitations with redemption of shares without shareholders' approvals where returns are to be via shareholders and limitations with respect to redeeming shares using capital.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is because of the need to satisfy the solvency requirements which are, on the whole, entity based.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Also, there is a limitation in relation to not being able to maintain the confidentiality of investments.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: VCCs are recognised under the DTAs as corporations that can benefit from the DTA agreements.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And this is a unique and significant advantage that funds domiciled in Singapore will get.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In particular, well-established regulations dealing with prevention of money laundering and terrorism financing apply to regulated fund managers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I do note, though, that there are two exempted classes of managers, namely, managers operating family offices and managers operating real estate assets.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The funds via VCCs themselves are regulated for AML via the proposed Part VII of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What steps can be taken to ensure that the level of supervision on these exempted managers is also comparable to regulated fund managers?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is because AML risks exist, vis-a-vis family office and real estate managers, too.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In relation to the re-domiciliation of funds, what would be the criteria to allow the migration?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I gather that, for companies, it is provided that there must be more than 50 employees, profits of more than $15 million or revenue of more than $50 million.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Recognising that fund vehicles have a long timespan, it is not unusual for fund vehicles to be operating for 10 years or more.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: So, what is the structural value proposition that Singapore can offer to fund managers to migrate their existing funds to Singapore?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And I believe this is a point that was made by the hon Member Ms Foo Mee Har as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Next, does the Government also intend to extend the corporate structure currently only usable for collective investment schemes to other spaces, for example, the insurance space, because the insurance companies also have segregated funds dealing with various insurance policies?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Or the securitisation space, because Singapore is also seeking to promote securitisation under the approved Special Purpose Vehicle Scheme.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Deputy Speaker, the new corporate structure VCC is attractive as it will provide greater flexibility for fund management companies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Before I go on, let me declare my interest.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, I am an employee of a local financial institution (FI).

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As the VCC structure allows it to issue and redeem shares without needing to seek shareholders' approval, investors may enter and exit from their investments freely.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It will make it easy for the fund manager to facilitate change of investors to meet business needs and keep pace with market practices.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is a vast improvement in addressing the problem of contagion risk.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is due to the issue of sub-funds having their own set of investors but the same legal personality, leading to the risk of assets and liabilities commingling.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the FIs be responsible for the KYC (Know your Client) process and SOW (Source Of Wealth) verification for each of the investors of that VCC or investors in the sub-funds?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If so, it may be necessary to allow FIs to have access to the information of the investors and shareholders if the authorities expect FIs with whom the account is opened to be compliant.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to ask what had been the number of disputes received so far from investors against fund managers in each of the last 10 years.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Singapore has a strong reputation as a safe, stable and well-regulated financial centre.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What measures are in place to eradicate scams and Ponzi schemes?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, competitiveness of the VCC framework as well as clarifications on its features.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, opportunities for local fund service providers and how we are working with them to capture these opportunities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And third, the potential impact on Singapore from a financial stability, risk and reputational standpoint.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Ms Foo Mee Har has highlighted, Singapore is, relatively speaking, a newcomer, competing with long-established fund domiciles, such as Luxembourg and Ireland.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We are able to take reference from tried and tested features of comparable structures, such as the UK and Ireland, so that our VCC framework is on par intentionally, and tailor the features to meet the needs of our industry.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For instance, the key advantage of our VCC framework is its enhanced flexibility to be used for both open-ended and close-end funds, and which are suitable across traditional and alternative investment strategies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This may not necessarily be available in other jurisdictions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Foo Mee Har raised feedback that giving sub-funds legal identities would be a more straightforward and effective way to ringfence their assets and liabilities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Internationally, corporate fund structures with cellular cells are structured either as protected cell companies (PCCs) or incorporated cell companies (ICCs).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The key difference between the PCC and ICC is whether sub-funds are accorded separate legal personalities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: While the ICC structure provides legal certainty over the status of its sub-funds, it has significant limitation in allowing umbrella funds to reap economies of scale and is, therefore, not conducive to the operation of investment funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For this reason, the PCC structure adopted by the VCC framework is also used in most international fund domiciles, such as the UK, Ireland and Luxembourg, whereas the ICC structure is only adopted in Guernsey.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Notwithstanding the lack of separate legal personality, VCCs are required under legislation to segregate assets and liabilities of sub-funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This will mitigate cross-cell contagion among sub-funds under the umbrella structure and, at the same time, ensure proper ringfencing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would also like to reassure Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Leon Perera that VCCs, including their sub-funds, can avail themselves of Singapore's competitive tax regime.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As announced by the Ministry of Finance (MOF) in its 2018 Budget Statement, a VCC will be treated as a company for tax purposes and will be allowed to enjoy our tax incentives for funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Leon Perera asked about sections 13R, 13X and 13Y of the Income Tax Act.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, section 13Y is not applicable as that is for prescribed sovereign entities and approved foreign government-owned entities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We intend for VCCs that are tax residents to access Singapore's tax treaties.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Tax residence of VCCs and their sub-funds are determined based on facts and circumstances.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To demonstrate that a VCC and its sub-funds are tax residents of Singapore, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) will issue a Certificate of Residence (COR) in the name of the VCC, with the names of the relevant sub-funds in the COR.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: More details on the tax treatment for VCCs will be released by the end of this year.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Foo Mee Har has also noted the importance of operational flexibility in closing down sub-funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, operational flexibility must be balanced against other considerations, including creditor protection.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As sub-funds have assets and liabilities attributable to them, we need a fair, orderly and robust procedure to deal with the legal issues and practical difficulties that may arise in the course of liquidating a sub-fund and distributing its assets.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Importantly, the legal obligations of parties in respect of a sub-fund's assets and liabilities must be clear.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The laws in general principles on corporate liquidation under the winding up provisions of the Companies Act (Cap 50) provide an established framework to ensure that the assets and affairs of sub-funds are dealt with in a fair and orderly manner.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Insolvency practitioners in Singapore are also familiar with the winding up regime under the Companies Act (Cap 50) and would be well-placed to act as liquidators of sub-funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Foo Mee Har has mentioned there could be room to further streamline processes and enhance operational efficiency with regard to the procedure for closing down sub-funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will study this and consider if there is a need to make further changes in subsequent legislative amendments.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Murali Pillai has asked whether it was intended for information relating to a particular sub-fund to be accessible by all shareholders of the VCC, including those who may not have interests in that sub-fund.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Under the Bill, a VCC's financial statements are required to be made available to all VCC shareholders.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Mr Murali Pillai pointed out, this would mean that financial information of individual sub-funds in an umbrella fund would be made available to all shareholders of the same VCC.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One of the main benefits of the VCC framework is its ability to be used as an umbrella fund with multiple sub-funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: By not restricting shareholders' access to financial information of sub-funds within an umbrella VCC, this brings about economies of scale, as sub-funds within the umbrella fund would be able to consolidate certain administrative functions, including the preparation of financial statements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For the same reason, a VCC will also be able to provide its financial information to prospective investors.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Such transparency will allow and encourage existing and prospective investors to monitor and assess the VCCs ' financial performance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They will be more informed and be able to hold fund managers to account.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In terms of shareholder privacy, a VCC is not required to provide a shareholder with information relating to its other shareholders.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: An investor in a particular sub-fund will not have the right, under the Bill, to obtain information, such as the identity and shareholding of another investor in the same sub-fund.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Murali Pillai has also asked about the criteria for overseas fund structures to re-domicile as VCCs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Moreover, imposing such minimum criteria for re-domiciling entities would restrict the entry for smaller funds, such as those investing in venture capital or those used to seed or launch a new strategy.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will provide further details on the operational process for re-domiciliation in the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Foo Mee Har has asked whether more can be done to facilitate the adoption by local funds of the VCC structure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will also study whether and how statutory mechanisms to facilitate the adoption of the VCC structure can be provided for in subsequent reviews.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The tax framework will be studied in tandem.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One of the key features of the framework is that the VCC may pay dividends using capital.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Leon Perera asked whether there are safeguards to make sure retail investors understand that the VCC may deplete its capital when paying such dividends.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In particular, funds that pay dividends out of capital are expected to disclose that dividends may be made out of capital and the implications of such dividends for investors.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will, as part its review of the funds’ documentation, check that such disclosures are made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Securities and Futures Act (Cap 289) requirements will apply to VCCs as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Looking ahead, Mr Murali Pillai has suggested that some of the features of the VCC framework, such as its ability to segregate assets and liabilities and avoid contagion risks between sub-funds, may benefit other financial activities, such as insurance-linked securities, insurance captives, assets securitisation and family offices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The VCC framework today is intended and designed for use as a corporate structure for investment funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I agree that some of the features could be useful for other applications.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Next, I will touch on the opportunities that the VCC framework will bring to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The introduction of the VCC framework will encourage fund managers to domicile their investment funds in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In turn, this will increase the pool of serviceable clients and create new work for local service providers, such as lawyers, auditors, fund administrators and fund custodians.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, a new fund setting up as a VCC in Singapore will need, first, lawyers to draft the fund's legal documents; second, fund administrators to assist with the day-to-day operations of the fund; and third, accountants to prepare and audit the financial statements of the fund.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The economic benefits rising from fund domiciliation will accrue to our local service providers and industry professionals.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Over the past year or so, MAS has worked closely with industry associations, local service providers and consultants to familiarise them with the value proposition and features of the VCC framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The fund management industry associations – Investment Management Association of Singapore (IMAS), Alternative Investment Management Association (AIMA) and Singapore Venture Capital Association (SVCA), as well as industry consultants, have provided useful feedback on the VCC framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They have partnered MAS to reach out to their members and clients through industry briefing sessions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will undertake more engagement sessions in the lead-up to the introduction of the VCC framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Specifically to Mr Saktiandi Supaat’s point about upskilling accountants, MAS has also been working with the auditing firms, as accountants will need to have the relevant competencies to support the preparation of financial statements of VCCs using either local or global accounting standards and principles.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will be issuing industry guidance notes prior to the launch to further support the practical implementation of the VCC framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether the Government will proactively engage foreign firm managers to come to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Murali Pillai also asked if we can incentivise fund managers to set up VCCs here.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Global asset managers, such as AIA Investment Management, which set up its first group-wide regional investment hub in Singapore, continue to anchor activities locally.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The VCC will play an important role in enhancing Singapore’s value proposition which includes a robust regulatory regime.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We believe foreign fund managers will find Singapore an attractive location to set up their operations and enjoy economies of scale from domiciling their funds in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether the flexibility accorded to investors to exit their investments in a VCC could cause disruptions or volatility to our economy.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This flexibility is not unique to VCCs and is available to fund investors today.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have recognised it is important for investors to have the flexibility to enter into or exit their investments at any point in time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS is very much aware of the risks and have taken steps to address them at the system and fund levels.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS closely monitors systemic risks to the economy, including those that may be caused by capital flows through investment funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Risks posed by the Singapore fund management sector to our financial markets are currently contained.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: A large part of assets under management in Singapore are invested outside Singapore, in the Asia Pacific region.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The VCC provides an alternative structure of fund vehicle.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But is not likely to significantly affect the investment behaviour of fund managers and investors.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Money invested in investment funds constituted as VCCs are therefore expected, in large part, to continue to be invested in assets overseas.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the fund level, all regulated fund managers, including those managing VCCs, are expected to put in place effective liquidity risk management frameworks and practices to ensure that their funds remain capable of fulfilling redemption requests in a timely manner when there are significant fund withdrawals.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Fund managers may also use liquidity management tools, such as suspension of redemptions and redemption gates, under exceptional circumstances, to pace out redemptions and help minimise the risk of transacting at-fire sale prices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Louis Ng has queried how we will safeguard against misconduct by VCCs and protect Singapore's international reputation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Murali Pillai has also asked how MAS can ensure risks relating to money laundering and financing of terrorism are managed, in particular, for certain managers that are not regulated by MAS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Safeguarding the integrity of our financial system against illicit funds and activities is paramount in ensuring that Singapore continues to be a financial centre trusted by international investors and global FIs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Singapore is committed to the global fight against money laundering and financing of terrorism.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We remain vigilant to the risk of abuse of our financial system as it grows in scale and sophistication.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This will help to ensure that the VCC shareholders are bona fide and will deter criminals from attempting to abuse the VCC for illicit purposes, including tax evasion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In practice, being primarily an investment vehicle, the VCC can choose to outsource this function to its fund manager or distributer, such as a bank.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, MAS will require VCCs to delegate the performance of AML/ CFT controls to an FI that is regulated and supervised by MAS for AML/CFT purposes, to be assured that VCCs are leveraging well-qualified firms to do these important checks.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The FIs to which these AML/CFT requirements are delegated will be required to obtain information on the VCC shareholders to the extent necessary for them to perform the delegated responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will consider providing further guidance on the eligible AML/CFT-regulated FIs which a VCC can delegate its AML/CFT requirements to.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I should highlight that the VCC is ultimately responsible for its own AML/CFT obligations, regardless of which FI the VCC outsources these functions to.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will adopt a risk-based supervisory approach, and higher-risk VCCs will be subject to closer scrutiny.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will not hesitate to take firm action against any VCC if AML/CFT controls are found to be inadequate.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, to ensure that VCCs are set up for legitimate purposes, there are requirements in the Bill as to who can manage them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: VCCs must appoint fund managers regulated by MAS and directors who are fit and proper to manage and give directions on its activities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Fundamentally, Singapore is a substantive economy, built on actual economic activities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The requirement for VCCs to be managed by fund managers regulated by MAS means that substantial fund management activities are already conducted in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Singapore works closely with the international community to deter the abuse of financial systems for the laundering of illicit funds, including proceeds of tax crimes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have also implemented international standards to combat base erosion and profit shifting (BEPS).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Under our laws, profits taxed in Singapore must comply with the international arm's length principle to ensure that profits commensurate with the actual economic activities conducted in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Singapore exchanges financial account information with a wide network of tax authorities in other jurisdictions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As regards Mr Gan Thiam Poh’s concerns about scams and Ponzi schemes, I would like to assure him that MAS continually renews its regulatory framework to safeguard the interests of retail investors.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, to enhance investor protection, amendments to the Securities and Futures Act (Cap 289) were passed by Parliament last year to provide MAS with greater flexibility and powers to bring non-conventional investment products within MAS’ regulatory parameters.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This was after MAS had observed that a number of non-conventional products, such as buyback arrangements involving gold or silver and plantation schemes, were deliberately structured to fall out of MAS' regulatory framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is an offence to operate a fraudulent or deceptive scheme.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are many channels by which MAS and other law enforcement agencies receive information on such suspicious investments, such as from members of the public, the financial industry, and other regulatory and enforcement agencies, local as well as overseas.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Where the information received suggest a breach of laws, the relevant authorities will investigate and will take appropriate action.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh also asked about the number of complaints against fund managers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These complaints generally relate to the closure of funds, fund performance or service matters, such as short notice given for submission of voting, collection of personal information, failure to receive statements of holdings.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We recognise, however, that no amount of regulation can prevent fraud.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ultimately, investors still need to exercise caution and evaluate the risks and features of any investment product or schemes offered, taking into account information available on these products or schemes, before making an investment decision.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I strongly encourage investors to deal only with entities regulated by MAS, and to consider the additional potential risks of dealing with investments and entities which are not regulated by MAS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS aims to safeguard the interests of consumers by ensuring that they are provided with adequate information to make more informed investment decisions and are dealt with fairly by financial intermediaries.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS has developed a number of resources on its website and through MoneySENSE, the national financial education programme, to share with the broader public common red flags of investment scams and that investors should be alerted to.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS will continue to work with industry, schools and other Government agencies to enhance financial literacy among Singaporeans so that they can make sound financial decisions.
